sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (federal-state allocation; English-French bilingual federal statutes; B.C. operates under statutory corporate registry law and the common law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada's network of Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) and 90+ Double Taxation Agreements, applicable according to ultimate beneficial owner nationality and residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.01 et seq.; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, as amended, including the transparency register and individuals with significant control provisions; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, if a federal CBCA entity is selected instead; FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons and sanctions; BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA) and Canadian Securities Administrators AML/CFT directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copy of passport (for each director and every individual holding 25% or more of shares)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin, or a BC notary if signed within Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the document originates in a Hague Apostille member state; otherwise consular legalization at the foreign consulate for use in Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank; notarized by an authorized public officer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the notarized copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank in country of origin; commissioned before a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate certificate of incumbency (where an intermediate corporate shareholder must be pierced)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or notary in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory verification of all directors, officers, and persons with significant control against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, United Nations sanctions lists, Canada's consolidated Criminal Code sanctions list, and FINTRAC guidance; mandatory detection of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence for high-risk persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and any nominee/intermediary arrangements; ongoing transaction monitoring and minimum 5-year record retention under PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (British Columbia Company Registry) via https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca; national NUANS name search via accredited NUANS search houses covering the federal and BC corporate databases.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Roman-alphabet letters; English and French forms of the distinctive element are preferred, with non-English names transliterated to align with BC naming conventions; the legal element may be 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or a French equivalent; numerals, hyphens, and invented words are permitted subject to statutory clarity and anti-confusion rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the BC Companies Office refuses a name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registries within 10 business days, citing the specific objection and offering a revised distinctive or descriptive element; if the administrative refusal remains, the applicant may file a new Name Request with an additional statutory fee or pursue judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia. A name reservation may be renewed before expiry, and third-party consent letters may be used to overcome conflicting-name objections.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office service is permissible in B.C. for a low-risk Amazon FBA merchant, provided the address is a physical street address in British Columbia, is not a post-office box, and is staffed during normal business hours to accept service of process; corporate service providers commonly provide the registered office and records office functions. The statutory registered office need not be the operational headquarters, but the company must maintain records at an accessible B.C. records office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated 5% probability of an unannounced registered-office inspection during the first 12 months for a standard low-risk marketplace seller with no trigger events; the likelihood rises to approximately 10-15% if FINTRAC/BCFSA conducts a targeted AML/CFT review or if the Canada Revenue Agency initiates a GST/HST or income tax audit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Global Affairs Canada or BC Ministry of Attorney General authentication office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff plus statutory authentication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: FINTRAC-registered service provider or law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GST/HST (federal) and BC PST registration preparation and filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 2-16, 21-52, 76-103, 128-143 (incorporation, share issuance, directors, registered and records office, annual reporting). Where a federal parallel structure is preferred, the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-15 applies and the company would additionally register as an extra-provincial company in British Columbia under Part 11 of the BCBCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Corporate Online Portal, Victoria, British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles (BC Form 1) together with Company Articles (or statutory default Articles) submitted electronically; Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The BCBCA imposes no statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital and no escrow account deposit requirement. One or more common shares may be subscribed and issued to incorporators for nominal consideration (e.g., CAD 1 per share). The authorized share structure, issue price, and share maximum are recorded in the Notice of Articles and share subscription schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers are appointed directors until the first annual general meeting and the Articles filed with the Notice of Articles are adopted. RESOLVED that the share subscription schedule is approved, shares are allotted and issued upon payment of the issue price, and share certificates are executed. RESOLVED that the registered and records office is established at [street address], Vancouver, British Columbia. RESOLVED that [Principal] is appointed President and CEO, [Officer] Secretary, and [Officer] CFO, each with authority to open bank and payment accounts and to file tax and statutory returns. RESOLVED that officers shall execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Corporate Online Name Request Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request using the NUANS electronic search through Corporate Online. Select a distinctive corporate name with an appropriate legal element (Inc., Corp., or Ltd.). Ensure the name is not confusingly similar to existing BC or federal corporate names. Pay the CAD 30 name request fee. A name reservation is valid for 56 days, which must cover the subsequent incorporation filing window.
required_dossiers: Payment of CAD 30 name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, file a revised name reservation with a distinctive new name within the same application session; a formal administrative review may be requested where the rejection is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or licensed British Columbia corporate law professional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles (Form 1), Articles, and initial director consents. The Notice of Articles must specify the corporate name, share classes and maximum share number, any share restrictions, the registered and records office address, and the first directors. The Articles may adopt the default statutory model or customized governance provisions. Ensure all directors execute written consents before filing.
required_dossiers: Written consents to act as director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a requisition for correction, revise and resubmit the Notice of Articles and Articles before the expiry of the name reservation; minor typographical errors may be cured by an amended filing without re-payment of the incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online with a BC Services Card or registered account. Enter the name reservation number, upload the prepared Notice of Articles and Articles, and pay the CAD 350 incorporation application fee by credit card. Upon validation, the Registrar files the Notice of Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically. The company comes into legal existence on the date of the Certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed BC Form 1 - Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for incomplete signatures or invalid share provisions, correct the deficiencies and refile promptly within the name reservation validity period; request a 28-day name reservation extension if additional correction time is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records Organization and Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary; Canada Revenue Agency; British Columbia Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate minute book, issue share certificates, and establish registers of directors, officers, and shareholders. Maintain the registered and records office at the address stated in the Notice of Articles. Register the company with the Canada Revenue Agency for the federal Business Number, GST/HST account, and corporate income tax. Register as a vendor for British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax if the company is deemed a vendor or marketplace seller. Obtain the municipal business licence applicable to the operating premises.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and share transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GST/HST or PST registration is late, apply through the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program to mitigate penalties and interest; no other material penalty applies if the first taxable sale has not yet occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Banking Mandate, and Annual Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Corporate Secretary; BC Corporate Registry Annual Report System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to adopt banking resolutions, authorize payment platform accounts (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex), establish the fiscal year-end, and approve the corporate governance calendar. File the annual report with the BC Corporate Registry no later than the anniversary of incorporation and pay the prescribed annual report fee. Ensure directors fulfill statutory duties and disclose any conflicts under the BCBCA.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Bank and payment platform signatory forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report is filed late, pay the late filing penalty and file immediately; if the company is dissolved for failure to file, apply for reinstatement under section 317 of the BCBCA within the statutory reinstatement period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Vancouver Licenses and Inspections Department for municipal business licensing; WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety registration; no provincial manufacturing licence applies to pure online marketplace retail.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Vancouver General Business Licence; British Columbia PST Marketplace Facilitator or Seller Registration; WorkSafeBC Employer Registration and Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is triggered for pure retail via internet marketplace and Amazon FBA fulfilment. The activity is categorically exempt under the Environmental Management Act unless warehouse premises exceed the regulatory size threshold or involve planned stormwater or waste discharges, in which case a registration or short-form notification may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous air pollutants arise from general e-commerce resale; any sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge bylaws and the BC Water Sustainability Act. Stormwater from warehouse and logistics sites must meet provincial water quality guidelines. Packaging and printed paper waste must comply with BC Recycling Regulation B.C. Reg. 449/2004, including extended producer responsibility obligations of upstream marketplace suppliers. Refrigeration equipment, if used, must comply with federal Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of warehouse or fulfilment premises in accordance with the BC Fire Code, including fire suppression systems, emergency egress, and electrical permits. Structural load inspection for pallet racking and mezzanine storage under the BC Building Code Section 4. WorkSafeBC workplace clearance and employer registration are required before any employees begin warehouse, logistics, or office operations, together with occupancy approval from the municipal building inspection department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal GST/HST and corporate income tax; British Columbia Consumer Taxation Branch for PST. Portal: CRA My Business Account / GST/HST NETFILE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register for a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account with the CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; a non-resident may appoint a Canadian representative via Form RC59. For BC PST, submit Application for Provincial Sales Tax Registration (FIN 418) to the BC Consumer Taxation Branch. Supporting documents include certified incorporation documents and evidence of Canadian business activities or nexus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and BC Income Tax Act. Non-resident corporations are taxed only on Canadian-source income (territorial scope for non-residents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective entity classification regime; classification is statutory. Except for procedural elections such as ITA s. 216 for net-basis taxation of Canadian rental income, there is no pass-through election. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.3 apply automatically and cannot be opted out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax; BC also imposes Provincial Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, CAD 30,000 in consideration for taxable supplies in Canada in a calendar quarter or four consecutive quarters (small supplier threshold). BC PST has no small-supplier monetary exemption; registration is required where a vendor has physical, agent, or directed-sales nexus in BC. Marketplace platform deeming rules may shift GST/HST collection obligations to operators such as Amazon.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing pre-clearance, or mandatory digital stamping regime. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1.5M must file electronically; voluntary Pan-Canadian Peppol-based e-invoicing is used for B2B transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act when exported in accordance with regulations and the supplier retains prescribed evidence such as CBSA Form B13A, bill of lading or air waybill, and commercial invoice showing the goods left Canada. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated when the recipient is not registered for GST/HST in Canada and the service is not primarily in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property located in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange settlement record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating, reassess within four years for ordinary errors and indefinitely for misrepresentation or fraud, and recover uncollected GST/HST plus interest and penalties. False statements or omissions in GST/HST returns may be subject to penalties under Exfise Tax Act s. 280 up to 250% of tax evaded, as well as criminal prosecution. Export evidence and accounting records must be retained for six years. Canada does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline; the operative controls are documentary evidence and accounting records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting jointly with the Department of Finance Canada on exchange-rate and monetary policy; Canada has abolished statutory foreign-exchange controls (the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951). The operative regulatory counterparts are the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federally incorporated banks, FINTRAC for cross-border transaction surveillance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and the Bank of Canada as administrator of the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) effective 1 November 2024.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in law and practice for both current and capital account items; Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and the Canadian dollar is free-floating. Profit remittance out of a British Columbia corporation is legally unrestricted, but four compliance gates apply: (i) Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) imposes 25% withholding on dividends, interest, rents, or royalties paid to non-residents, treaty-reduced under the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention to generally 15% on portfolio dividends, 5% on a U.S. corporate shareholder owning 10% or more, and generally 0% on arm's-length interest; (ii) the corporation's bank, not the corporation, reports electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period to FINTRAC; (iii) the payment must not breach sanctions lists administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Criminal Code; and (iv) corporate treasury policy must document the funding chain to avoid recharacterisation of shareholder loans as unremittable or tax-non-compliant equity. There is no repatriation permit, no currency allocation, and no central-bank clearance for outbound treasury payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export proceeds, including Amazon Seller Central payout receipts in CAD, USD, or other marketplaces. A Canadian exporter may retain proceeds in any currency. Ancillary compliance includes: (a) CBSA export declarations for physical exports from Canada above the current Customs Act reporting threshold of CAD 2,000; (b) for FBA inventory purchased offshore and shipped directly to Amazon fulfilment centres, the Canadian seller must act as importer of record and instruct a licensed customs broker, but no import licence is required for general merchandise; and (c) for Canadian income tax purposes, foreign-currency balances must be translated in the financial statements and gains/losses from retranslation of foreign-currency receivables and payables are taxable or deductible under subsection 39(1) of the Income Tax Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD with RBC Bank Georgia routing) plus segregated Capital Escrow Account for share-subscription proceeds
Operational Account (CAD/USD via TD Bank N.A.) plus segregated Capital Escrow Account for paid-in capital
Operational Account (CAD/USD via BMO Harris Bank) plus segregated Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (CAD/USD via Scotiabank U.S.) plus Capital Escrow Account for investor deposits
Operational Account (CAD/USD via CIBC U.S. presence) plus Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (CAD), limited U.S.-dollar clearing; capital escrow available on request

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for settlement and FX conversion, subject to legal constraints. Airwallex (Canada) Ltd., Wise Solutions Canada Inc., and Payoneer Inc. (Canada branch) are all FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses and either hold or are in process of holding Retail Payment Activities Act registration with the Bank of Canada. They may lawfully hold client funds in safeguarded trust accounts at Schedule I banks, provide multi-currency accounts (USD, CAD, CNH), and connect to Amazon disbursement rails. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a deposit-taking institution under the Bank Act and cannot offer deposit insurance or term deposits; (ii) the RPAA registration obligation applies to any payment service provider operating in Canada, so a foreign EMI without Canadian registration cannot legally facilitate the seller's receipts; (iii) the EMI must remain a payment mechanical layer only - the BC corporation must remain the merchant of record and registered GST/HST registrant for supply under the Excise Tax Act, since the EMI is not a reseller and cannot alter place-of-supply; and (iv) if Amazon payouts are routed through an EMI, the seller should obtain an IRS W-8BEN-E and the EMI's 'local receiving account' details to evidence that Amazon is paying the Canadian entity and not an unregistered intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not mandatory in law. Neither the Bank Act, the PCMLTFA, nor the BC Business Corporations Act requires a director to appear physically at a Canadian branch to open a corporate operating account. For a low-risk domestic e-commerce corporation with a Canadian-resident director, the major banks accept fully remote onboarding using digital identity verification (government-issued photo ID plus liveness check) and an electronically signed corporate resolution. However, where a director or 25%+ beneficial owner is a non-resident individual, most banks apply Enhanced Due Diligence and will require either an in-branch interview at a Canadian branch, a remote video interview with compliance, or a notarised identity declaration certified before a notary public in the director's country with apostille or consular legalisation, plus a banker's reference from the director's home bank. A corporate attorney or authorised signatory may complete the interview process under a BC Power of Attorney, but the bank retains discretion to request physical attendance if the sanctions screen produces an ambiguous match or if any UBO is in a FATF-high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial onboarding of a newly incorporated BC shelf corporation with no trading history, no website, no filed tax returns, and nominal paid-in capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles from the BC Corporate Registry; corporate by-laws; list of directors and officers with government-issued photo ID; Amazon Seller Central registration certificate and live store URL; detailed e-commerce business plan covering product sourcing, FBA logistics, and projected margins; pro-forma cash-flow statement; CRA Business Number confirmation letter; and, where applicable, the engagement letter of a licensed customs broker evidencing future cross-border inventory flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A single large inbound credit from Amazon's pooled disbursement account aggregating thousands of unrelated consumer card payments, raising suspicion of transaction laundering or unlicensed money-services business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon Services Business Solutions Agreement; Amazon Seller Central account statement identifying the payout reference; monthly settlement reports with order-level detail; a reconciliation mapping the pooled payout to individual orders; confirmation that Amazon acts as payment facilitator and merchant of record; a sworn funds-flow narrative; and the seller's internal ledger showing that no consumer payment is accepted directly by the Canadian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid pass-through pattern: USD FBA receivables arriving and being wired within one to three days to a Chinese supplier without supporting trade documents, a classic trade-based money-laundering indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders and commercial invoices matching each wire; bill of lading or master air waybill consignment notes for FBA inbound shipments; CBSA customs entry data (B3 customs coding) or customs-broker reports; transfer-pricing memorandum evidencing arm's-length pricing; inventory-purchase ledger; cash-conversion-cycle narrative; supplier KYC pack including the supplier's business licence, bank confirmation, and sanctions-screening clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or 25%+ beneficial owners domiciled in a high-risk or FATF-monitored jurisdiction, or ownership through an offshore holding entity, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies and proof of residential address for every director and UBO; apostilled police clearance or banking reference from the home-country bank; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements covering the initial capital; corporate registry extracts (certificate of incorporation and register of directors) for each corporate shareholder; a signed FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership declaration; and an organisational chart showing the ultimate natural-person controllers of CA_CORP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office or PO-box address only, with no physical Canadian presence or operational substance for the business corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or sublease for a physical premises in British Columbia, or a registered-office-services contract with a law firm or registered agent; utility or ISP bill in the corporation's name; municipal business licence (if any) categorised as retail sale via internet; third-party logistics or Amazon FBA warehouse contracts; payroll records, if employees exist; and bank statements showing expected settlement activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin-capitalisation shareholder loans: large non-resident shareholder advances with no interest, no repayment schedule, and no documentation, suggesting disguised equity or tax avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed interest-bearing loan agreement or promissory note at the CRA prescribed rate in effect at drawdown; board resolution approving the commercial purpose of the loan; interest drawdown and repayment schedule; debt-to-equity calculation demonstrating compliance with the Income Tax Act thin-capitalisation safe harbour (generally 1.5:1 debt-to-equity for specified non-resident shareholders); accounting entries under IFRS or ASPE; and a Part XIII withholding plan with completed CRA Form NR301 or NR302 for any interest payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan protocol: (i) Corporate authority - a board resolution of the BC corporation authorising the share subscription or the shareholder loan, and confirmation that the Notice of Articles authorises the share class to be issued; BC law imposes no minimum paid-up capital, and the wire may be credited directly to the operational account or to a designated Capital Escrow Account. (ii) Wire standard - SWIFT MT103 containing field 50K (ordering customer: the foreign shareholder), field 59 (beneficiary: CA_CORP at the Canadian Schedule I bank, full account number and BIC), and field 70 (remittance information, e.g. 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - RESOLUTION DATED - SHARE CERTIFICATE NO. X' or 'LOAN PRINCIPAL UNDER PROMISSORY NOTE DATED'). For USD wires originating in the U.S., use Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's U.S. affiliate; for CAD wires, use LVTS or the emerging Real-Time Rail. (iii) Purpose codes - Canada has no statutory purpose-code directory; the receiving bank internally classifies the credit as 'capital contribution' or 'intercompany loan' for AML purposes, and the sender should reference the transaction ID or loan agreement number. (iv) Verification and reporting - the bank collects the corporate KYC pack and, for any single or aggregated cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more in 24 hours, the bank files the FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report; the non-resident shareholder should provide Form W-8BEN-E or a treaty-residency certificate to support future interest or dividend withholding relief. (v) Tax-compliant credit - a shareholder loan must bear interest at the CRA prescribed rate to preserve deductibility and avoid deemed-benefit rules; share-subscription proceeds are not taxable and no stamp duty or capital duty applies; if the shareholder is a U.S. person, the issuance should comply with the BC Securities Act private-issuer exemption under NI 45-106 (restriction on transfer and a maximum of 50 security holders).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade clearing rails: (i) Supplier T/T - SWIFT MT103 from the Canadian bank to the beneficiary supplier bank in USD, CNH, or CAD; field 70 must include the invoice number, purchase-order number, and the phrase 'PURCHASE OF INVENTORY - TRADE PAYMENT' to avoid misrepresentation; the bank applies OSFI-required sanctions screening, and FINTRAC EFT reporting triggers at CAD 10,000 or more in 24 hours. (ii) Commercial letters of credit - for large FBA inventory replenishment, issue an irrevocable documentary credit via SWIFT MT700 from the Canadian issuing bank to the supplier's confirming bank, payable at sight (MT700 field 42P 'SIGHT') or by deferred payment (field 42P 'DEF'); required documents include the signed commercial invoice, full set of clean-on-board bills of lading or air waybill, packing list, certificate of origin, and any inspection certificate; if goods are destined to an Amazon fulfilment centre in the U.S., the U.S. ISF/ACE entry filings must be consistent with the LC document descriptions and the Canadian seller must remain importer of record. (iii) Settlement systems - high-value CAD payments clear via Payments Canada LVTS; USD payments clear through CHIPS or Fedwire; same-day cross-currency settlement may be achieved through CLS where the selected bank is a CLS settlement member. (iv) Amazon payout rail - the corporation should maintain a dedicated USD 'FBA settlement account' at the bank's U.S. affiliate or at a FINTRAC-registered EMI such as Airwallex or Payoneer to segregate Amazon disbursements from trade payables and to enable the treasury to apply a natural CAD/USD hedge before layering any derivative.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward on CAD/USD and USD/CNH booked with a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement (BC-govened) with a Credit Support Annex; available to end-user corporate hedgers without OSFI approval and without exchange-control permission.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on USD/CNY where deliverable CNY is unavailable to the Canadian seller; booked offshore in USD with a Canadian bank's NDF desk; requires an ISDA 2002 NDF annex and is permissible where the underlying commercial invoice is denominated in CNY and the BC corporation settles in USD.

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swap (FX swap) between CAD and USD, used to bridge mismatched Amazon disbursement cycles and working-capital obligations; must be supported by an internal hedge-authorisation memorandum and board delegation.

Vanilla European-style FX options (CAD calls / USD puts) as a premium-based hedging overlay, permissible for end-user corporates in Canada and subject to the same ISDA and credit-limit framework as forwards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (BCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / BC Registry Online
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 2 months after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late-filing penalty; failure to file for 2 consecutive years empowers the Registrar to dissolve the company administratively under BCA s. 273; the company is also barred from commencing or defending legal proceedings while in default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and BC provincial corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax payable generally due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest at prescribed rates; CRA may issue arbitrary assessments and suspend compliance-related payments or refunds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST remitters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty up to CAD 2,500; interest at prescribed rates; CRA may assess net tax and apply penalties for willful non-compliance under the Excise Tax Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold under BC BCA for private companies; an independent auditor is required unless all shareholders pass an annual unanimous resolution waiving the audit. Public companies must appoint an auditor and cannot waive this requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as Canadian private-enterprise GAAP; private e-commerce corporations commonly apply ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under BCA Part 2.1, each BC private company must maintain a Transparency Register identifying significant individuals with 25% or greater ownership/control; the annual BC Annual Report requires confirmation that the register is complete, accurate, and up to date. Changes in significant individuals must be recorded in the register and reflected in the next annual confirmation; separate UBO filing is not required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register of Significant Individuals (BC BCA Part 2.1)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110 - 520 per annum (CAD 150 - 700) for BC registered office / registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 11,000 per annum for a small private e-commerce corporation if an audit is required; nil if audit waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined federal and British Columbia general corporate income tax rate (15% federal Part I basic rate after provincial abatement and general rate reduction + 12% BC provincial rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: first CAD 500,000 of active business income taxed at 11% combined (9% federal + 2% BC). Foreign tax credits, SR&ED investment tax credits, and manufacturing/processing deductions may further reduce effective tax. No statutory tax holidays are available for general internet retail trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (CRA form, integrated federal and BC provincial return). Filed electronically via CRA-approved software using EFILE, Taxprep, or comparable commercial tax filing portal; effectively every corporate tax filer must e-file unless exempt.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly tax instalment payments are required in advance for most corporations whose instalment obligations exceed CAD 3,000. The annual T2 return covering the fiscal period is filed once per year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 must be filed no later than six calendar months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year. For a December 31 year-end, the deadline is June 30. The final balance-due day is two months after the fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs and certain CCPCs, and three months after year-end for CCPCs eligible for the small business deduction in that year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, CRA Business Number (BN), federal/provincial incorporation number or governing BC registration, fiscal year-end date, mailing address, and principal business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian resident entity's BN; do not substitute the foreign parent's tax ID. Indicate if the corporation is controlled by non-residents for statutory classification purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross worldwide sales, commissions, delivery income, Amazon Seller Central receipts, and other commercial revenue. Amazon FBA gross sales must be reported in Canadian dollars at the applicable daily exchange rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income of the Canadian corporation. Foreign-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment in a treaty country may be deducted, provided a meaningful PE exists and the tax treaty is invoked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less cost of goods sold, including Amazon FBA fulfilment fees, storage fees, referral fees, and amortized inventory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing file for any related-party Amazon service fees or offshore service agreements; only costs attributable to the Canadian operation are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, marketing, warehouse costs, professional fees, interest, royalties, depreciation, and administrative expenses. Non-deductible club dues or unreasonable compensation attract reassessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose any management or royalty fees paid to non-residents on Form T106; Part XIII withholding tax must be withheld unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before tax, reduced by loss carryforwards, dividends received deduction, foreign non-business income deductions, and the small business deduction allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only treaty-protected PE income and foreign-source amounts qualify for deductions; non-resident shareholders are not taxed directly on Canadian corporate income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax calculated at the basic 38% rate, reduced by the 10% provincial abatement and the 13% General Rate Reduction to yield the 15% federal general rate; for CCPCs, the Small Business Deduction reduces the effective federal rate to 9% on eligible active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same federal rate applies irrespective of shareholder residence. Provincial abatement is available only where the corporation has a permanent establishment in a province.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: British Columbia corporation tax at 12% general rate, or 2% on active business income eligible for the BC small business deduction. Income is allocated to BC based on actual revenue and payroll factors for corporations with permanent establishments outside BC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are subject to BC tax only if they have a permanent establishment in BC; Amazon FBA inventory stored in BC by third-party warehousing does not, by itself, create a BC PE for the seller.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: T106 reports all reportable transactions with non-residents, including cross-border contract values, associated parties, and the prescribed transfer pricing method. T1135 discloses foreign income properties such as foreign bank accounts, foreign affiliates, and offshore trust holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory where annual intercompany transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000, or where foreign property with a cost above CAD 100,000 is held at any time in the year. Non-resident-owned Canadian entities, including treaty-protected corporations, remain subject to these reporting obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% for each full month of delinquency, up to 12 months (maximum 17%). For a second or subsequent offence within three years: 10% plus 2% per month, up to 20 months (maximum 50%). Daily compound interest is charged at the CRA prescribed rate (updated quarterly). Failure to file Form T106 attracts a penalty of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000; failure to file T1135 attracts a minimum CAD 2,500 penalty, increasing to CAD 25,000 for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident of Canada, subject to reduction under an applicable income tax convention.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident payee must be the beneficial owner of the dividend and must provide the Canadian paying corporation with a valid foreign tax authority residence certificate and, where applicable, CRA Form NR301 or NR302 (Statement of Entitlement to Treaty-Prescribed Reduced Rate). The payer must withhold at the treaty-reduced rate before payment; documentation must be received in time. For dividends paid to a US resident, the general treaty rate is 15%, reduced to 5% for a company that owns at least 10% of the voting shares of the payer. For other treaty partners, consult the specific DTA. If documentation is insufficient, the statutory 25% must be withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding tax on royalties and interest is 25%. Under the Canada-US tax treaty, arm's-length interest paid to a US resident is exempt from source withholding (0%); industrial royalties (patents, trademarks, know-how) are generally capped at 10%, and cultural or artistic copyright royalties at 0%. Where no treaty applies, the statutory 25% rate applies to royalties and interest, except for certain statutory exemptions for arm's-length interest on government obligations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in annual aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents requires mandatory Form T106 and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (local-file equivalent). A multinational group consolidated revenue threshold of CAD 750,000,000 triggers Master File and Country-by-Country Report filing obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Instead, economic substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Act, s.245), the common-law 'sham' doctrine, and residency rules based on central management and control. A Canadian e-commerce corporation that is a letterbox or 'post-box' entity, without real board activity, employees, contracts, or commercial decisions in Canada, is exposed to recharacterization by CRA. Amazon FBA storage alone in a foreign jurisdiction does not, without more, create a foreign permanent establishment; however, the substantive control of the seller must remain in Canada to sustain Canadian-resident status and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Amazon FBA gross receipts, fabricating cost of goods sold, inflating advertising or fulfilment deductions, or neglecting to report sales parked in an offshore bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under section 163(2) of the Income Tax Act of 50% of the understated tax; daily compound interest on the unreported balance; criminal conviction under section 239(1) for tax evasion carries imprisonment up to 5 years upon indictment and fines up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded. Repeated failure to file carries added s.162(1) penalties of 10% plus 2% per month to a 50% ceiling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporation is used as a mere instrumentality, the court and CRA will pierce the corporate veil; directors and officers who participated in the evasion become personally liable for the corporate tax debt, are subject to civil restitution proceedings, can be criminal defendants, and may face travel bans or seizure of passports under CRA collection measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing goods sold to a related offshore FBA trader, overpaying a related Hong Kong or Singapore service company for 'Amazon consultancy' fees, or assigning valuable Canadian-developed trademarks to a tax-haven subsidiary at a nominal price.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment to an arm's-length compensation under s.247(2); transfer-pricing penalty under s.247(11) equal to 10% of the net upward adjustment where the taxpayer did not prepare adequate contemporaneous documentation. Failure to file T106 is an additional CAD 100-per-day penalty up to CAD 25,000; interest on the reassessment is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing certificates or who orchestrate the artificial transfer of assets are personally liable under criminal fraud and conspiracy provisions. The corporate veil is pierced, allowing CRA to trace and seize the director's personal assets and to impose civil penalties equal to the unpaid corporate tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pre-registered, non-operating Canadian 'shelf' corporation with no employees, no local bank operation, and no substantive management decision-making, where real control and e-commerce management sit offshore, solely to claim Canadian residence and treaty-derived tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The transaction or entity is disregarded under s.245 (GAAR), and income is reattributed to the actual controlling foreign person. The resulting deemed dividends or royalties to non-residents attract Part XIII withholding tax at 25%, plus gross-negligence penalties and interest. The sham determination is retroactive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited liability is lost when the corporation is no longer a genuine commercial enterprise. Shareholders/directors become personally liable for the full Canadian tax liability; CRA may register a lien against personal assets, impose an emigration/exit ban, and seek personal civil recovery where the controlling person has absconded with corporate funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) for a foreign bank account or foreign affiliate while holding Amazon sales proceeds in a US$ offshore account, or failing to register with FINTRAC when acting as a money-services business; laundering e-commerce proceeds through digital assets or shell corporations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.162(7), T1135 non-filing or false reporting is subject to a penalty of CAD 2,500 per failure, with CAD 25,000 for gross negligence. Under the Criminal Code of Canada, money laundering carries a maximum fine of CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years; FINTRAC administrative penalties can reach CAD 500,000 for money-services businesses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly divert or hide foreign financial assets are personally exposed to criminal money-laundering prosecution and civil liability. CRA can freeze their personal accounts, issue travel bans, and pierce the corporate veil where the corporation served as a laundering conduit; the director is jointly and severally liable for all unremitted source deductions and income tax arising from the scheme.
